title.narrative: Support to Implementation of the Bangladesh Delta Plan 2100 (SIBDP2100).

description.narrative:
The main aim of the SIBDP2100 project is to prepare and support the implementation of the Bangladesh Delta Plan 2100 by providing Policy Advice (including institutional development, funding strategy, river basin wise implementation programming) and Capacity Building (including communication and stakeholder participation, training, information and knowledge management).
The Bangladesh Delta Plan (BDP) 2100 focuses primarily on adaptation to climate change and on foodsecurity and economic development. The BDP2100 provides a long term vision, goals and strategies, an institutional framework and investment plan. It was formulated from 2014-2018 in a multi sectoral way by the General Economics Division, Planning Commision of the Ministry of Planning, supported by an international consortium led by Dutch consultancy firm Twynstra Gudde Holding B.V. The project was funded by the Government of the Netherlands. BDP2100 was approved by the National Economic Council (NEC), presided over by the Prime Minister and Chairperson of the NEC, on 4 September 2018. Bangladesh is the first country in the world to develop such a comprehensive multi-sectoral plan including an investment plan for the entire delta, using Adaptive Delta Management. The Government has assigned the General Economics Division (GED) the responsibility of the overall coordination, facilitation and monitoring of the BDP 2100 implementation.
The Government of the Kingdom of the Netherlands has extended the financial support to operationalize BDP2100 in a TA project, entitled "Support to the Implementation of the Bangladesh Delta Plan 2100 (SIBDP2100)". A team of consultants of the SIBDP consortium with lead partner Twynstra Gudde Holding B.V. has been engaged to support GED in its tasks of initiating and coordinating BDP2100 implementation with other ministries and implementing agencies, with effect from 1 October 2018. The consortium consists, besides Twynstra Gudde Holding B.V., of Deltares and Euroconsult Mott MacDonald and sub-contractors Institute of Water Modelling (IWM), Center for Environmental and Geographic Information Services (CEGIS) , Climate Adaptation Foundation (CAS).

organisation.narrative:
TwynstraGudde Holding B.V.
TwynstraGudde Holding B.V. is an independent Dutch management consultancy firm, active amongst others in areas as water safety, security and governance; climate change adaptation including transformative policy making, master planning and implementation; infrastructure development and sustainable transportation; energy transition; spatial development. Characteristic advisory services are based on policy analysis, development and reflective evaluation; strategic management and (long term) planning, transformation and strategic change; institutional analysis and development; leadership, organization structuring and change, program and project management, asset management, stakeholder participation. Training and capacity building programs are based on these skills and experiences.

SIBDP support consists of various forms of capacity building. The main focus of the project concerns enhancing the 5 following implementation capacities: 1. Institutional and Administrative Capacity 2. Connective and Organization Capacity 3. Knowledge and Learning Capacity 4. Funding Capacity 5. Natural System Adaptive Capacity
The focus of the Results on Capacity Building is on all 5 items, which have been elaborated in national and international training programme, workshops, fieldtrips as well as building capacity for knowledge management including the Knowledge and Information Portal.

title.narrative: SIBDP Annual Plan 2022. This document shows also progress on the various aspects of capacity building.

description.narrative:
Strengthening of main Delta Plan Institutions and Agencies A Focal Point network has already been formed to support and promote coordination and collaboration of GED with involved ministries and agencies. A next step is required to anchor BDP2100 actions firmly by formation of Delta Cells. SIBDP supports defining the tasks and mandate, by further training, frequent Focal Point Meetings and requests for data exchange. Formation of Delta Cells means creating a unit in the involved ministries or agencies consisting of senior planning officials. Such a Delta Cell has been formed within BWDB. Some core implementation institutions, especially BWDB, DAE and LGED require assistance for BDP2100 implementation with a focus on: (a) BDP2100 content and funding; (b) the upcoming implementation tasks and (c) the needs of the organizations to make BDP implementation achievable. SIBDP will form working groups in which the BDP2100 Implementation Programs will be used for project selection and preparation (see also Par. 2.5.). A conference on BDP2100 implementation with 300 participants has been held together with BWDB on 27 October 2021 in which challenges and needs were identified. Besides, the Convention of Diploma Engineers and SIBDP organized a large Conference (750 participants) on BDP2100 and implementation implications. Further elaboration of the findings of both Conferences is required in 2022 to overcome continuing implementation issues e.g. at MoWR / BWDB in terms of readiness to implement which includes project preparation from Concept Notes to bankable projects. This also concerns the planning function of BWDB in relation to GED and WARPO. Moreover, an International Conference on BDP2100 Implementation will be held possibly 11 and 12 May 2022 to address implementation issues and to develop a meaningful course of action. SIBDP supports the preparation of this first International Conference and coordinates and contributes to the formulation of the Conference Paper.
Training
The responsibility for the implementation of the domestic trainings lies with GED. GED provided on-line trainings to Focal Points twice as well as on-line trainings for GoB officials. SIBDP assists in identifying and preparing the training modules and material and facilitating the online sessions. The three short international training courses in European countries or in Australia and two courses in Asian or African countries will be organized and funded by GoB. GED intends to arrange two International Certificate Courses. SIBDP supports identifying the suitable courses as soon as the Delta Wing has been formed. SIBDP provides in principle two international study tour/ training programs. In order to make international training effective, the events will be provided for the Delta Wing staff (possibly 2 events combined in 1 or a course to be arranged in Bangladesh). It is expected and in the budget as such included, that under the Covid19 circumstances international trainings will not be possible before the end of the SIBDP project on 30 September.
SIBDP provided training on Appraising BDP2100 and Adaptive Delta Management to 189 officers during FY 2020-2021 and 98 officers in FY 2021-2022. Technical and online support was provided to many meetings and workshops during the Covid19 period. Due to outbreak of Covid19, the pre-scheduled trainings, seminars and workshops by physical presence got postponed. However, using online platforms, SIBDP has completed 3 workshops, 2 workshops cum training and 8 short trainings (3-4 days training). Besides, SIBDP contributed significantly to the Conference on Blue Gold project; to the Conference on BDP2100 with BWDB (300 participants); the Conference on BDP2100 with the Convention of Diploma Engineers (900 participants). Further information has been included in the Progress Reports and the Project Completion Report.
The Project Completion Report summarizes the SIBDP-TA activities and shows what has been achieved in terms of prepared and submitted reports, trainings, workshops etc.
The SIBDP Results overview gives an overview of deliverables and achievements already done or in progress. The overview focuses on 5 implementation capacities.
The Report over 2021 shows progress on the 5 Capacities and a risk analysis and possible measures to be taken.

title.narrative: Knowledge Management - knowledge development, sharing and accumulation

description.narrative: Knowledge Management concerns all 5 Implementation Capacity areas in the form of data collection, analysis and reporting. Furthermore, setting knowledge available on request by GED or others, based on proper archiving and document management or by collecting information. The Knowledge and Information Portal needs to be further developed and updated to be informative and contain many data collections / layers and documents.

target.value: Increased information and communication about BDP2100 including content related data layers, information and communication outputs, reports and proposals. Attentiona needs to be paid to availability and accessability of the knowledge and data on a dedicated Knowledge Portal.

actual.value: High progress on SIBDP side in terms of preparations and performed activities. Knowledge Management has taken place on all 5 Implementation Capacity areas in the form of data collection, analysis and reporting. Furthermore, setting knowledge available on request by GED or others, based on proper archiving and document management or by collecting information. A BDP2100 documentary has been prepared and used many times, as well as information brochures and other communication material. The Knowledge and Information Portal has been established and updated and contains many data collections / layers and documents. At GoB/GED, a dedicated room has been developed to host the Knowledge Portal with provided server and necessary internet, protection and other IT-equipment. See the uploaded Results Overview.

description.narrative: Reaching out to stakeholders by informing them based on video, borchures etc. and involving them in workshops, conferences and preparation of deliverables. Consultation took place in the form of workshops and Delta Ateliers during the Implementation Programming. Besides, officials of the implementing agencies including the Focal Point network were consulted on many occasions with respect to SIBDP activities and deliverables.

target.value: Increased communication, participation and consultation of stakeholders, experts and interested people.

actual.value: High progress on SIBDP side in terms of preparations and performed communication, participation and consultation activities. Fruitful communication took place in many workshops and meetings, in which the documentary and brochures etc. were used. A number of large BDP2100 focused conferences were organized: with the Blue Gold Project on Participatory Water Institutions, the BDP2100 International Conference, the Conference with the Institution of Diploma Engineers Bangladesh, Conference with Bangladesh Water Development Board. Delta Ateliers were held in 5 places concerning the basin wise programming. Many reports were published, reviewed and expert meetings were held on submitted reports. See the uploaded Results Overview.

description.narrative: SIBDP developed the training strategy and contents, provided trainings, developed training modules and supported to training by GED. For international training/ study tour, a tentative program has been prepared.

target.value: Increased understanding and insights as well as knowledge of BDP 2100 and related concepts and Investment Plan.

actual.value: High progress on SIBDP side in terms of provided trainings and training module preparations and related performed activities. International training was not possible so far due to Covid19. See the uploaded Results Overview.

description.narrative: SIBDP-TA supported implementation of BDP2100 in the form of Policy Advices on various with implementation related issues. Progress has been indicated in the uploaded progress reports. The results up to 31 December 2023 have been indicated in the Project Completion Report. The results have been specified according to support on 5 Capacities: 1. Institutional and Administrative 2. Connective and Organization 3. Knowledge and Learning 4. Funding 5. National System Adaptive Capacity Policy Advice relates to these 5 capacities.

The Extension Work Plan builds on the assumption that normalization of SIBDP-activities continues in the course of 2022 and 2023. The Annual Plan 2022 contains activities on the five Implementation Capacities which will be finalized in the extension period. In addition, recommendations of the EKN approval letter on the SIBDP Annual Plan 2022 including MTR-suggestions will be followed. The extension activities are indicated in Chapter 2. Chapter 3 briefly explores risks related to realization of the expected outcomes and indicates possible measures. The budget neutral extension is presented in Chapter 4 as financial forecast for the period of October 2022 - June 2023.

title.narrative: Result overview of SIBDP achievements as per May 2022.

description.narrative: The SIBDP Narrative Report 2020 gives an overview of Activities and the Result overview shows deliverables already done or in draft form. The Result overview focuses on 5 implementation capacities.

The SIBDP Progress report 2022 covers the final part of the original contract up to 30 September 2022. Delays due to COVID-19 were managed but extension was required to complete the tasks. EKN decided for a budget neutral extension till 30 June 2023. The Extension Workplan has been uploaded separately.

The SIBDP-TA Project Completion Report (PCR) provides an overall view from TA-side of SIBDP in terms of background of the BDP 2100 and implementation aspects. BDP 2100 is a comprehensive long term plan which requires attention for implementation readiness. SIBDP-TA worked on this readiness to implement by developing and improving five implementation capacities. The issues and challenges during the working process have been addressed including the COVID-19 circumstances. The PCR shows that expected deliverables have been realized and submitted to GED/ GOB. The PCR presents an overview of the capacities and what has been done and delivered. The Annexes of the PCR present lists with reports, trainings and other achievements.

This proposal elaborates on the by EKN requested extension (mail of 17th May 2023) of the TA team part of SIBDP as requested by GED. The proposal is in line with the SIBDP Extension Work Plan 2022-2023 (no new items included) which has been formulated to support and guide GED with the implementation of BDP 2100. The SIBDP Progress Report indicates the progress up to early 2023 and signals that the intended deliverables will be finalized in time but that interaction with GED and implementing institutions has been limited. The overall transition process is still ongoing and requires further interactions and assistance. Considering EKN’s request, the SIBDP-project focuses during this extension period on guidance and related tools, with further interaction on and elaboration of existing deliverables. The submitted reports require explanation or training at and processing by GED. Especially dissemination to and interaction with involved ministries and agencies through the Focal Point network is urgently needed, followed by joint elaboration of received contributions. By doing this, the working procedures of the Delta Wing and other parts of the institutional framework will be utilized and where needed improved.

The Institutional and Administrative Capacities increased by development and operationalization of the institutional framework and knowledge sharing and dedicated training. See the uploaded documents for progress and final results.

The Knowledge and Learning Capacity was increased by developing the Knowledge and Information Portal and transferring it to GED including training. Besides the meta model development and application in two regional programmes including dedicated training contributed to this capacity. Further more, knowledge was developed and applied on GCF and PPP as well during the regional programming. See for the overview of results and deliverables the uploaded Progress Reports and Project Completion Report.

The Natural System Adaptive Capacity has been increased in the first place by translating the BDP 2100 into regional, basin wise programmes with analysis of the basin characteristics in which interventions would take place. Besides, additional proposals and Investment Plan has been delivered. Operations and Maintenance was elaborated in a Policy Brief on O&M. Moreover, Asset Management and Rationalization projects have been highlighted. Proposals were prepared for the GCF in interaction with the related authorities. See for the overview of results and deliverables the uploaded Progress Reports and Project Completion Report.

The Organization and Connective Capacity increased by development and operationalization of the institutional framework with the Focal Points and related ministries and stakeholders. Capacity strengthening took place through knowledge sharing and many trainings, partly online. See the uploaded documents for progress and final results.

The funding capacity increased in the first place by the policy brief on a Delta Fund. Secondly, GCF and PPP have been explored on possibilities and actual proposals. Third, the beneficiary pay principle was elaborated with respect to possible contributions for delivered water services. Fourth, relations with development Partners and IFIs were developed in relation to BDP 2100 and its implementation challenges. See for the overview of results and deliverables the uploaded Progress Reports and Project Completion Report.
